subject: Media Literacy
title: Censorship and Press Freedom
description: One-minute skill: Censorship and Press Freedom.

hook.text: Every government that saw the printing press immediately tried to control it.

buildup.text: England required printers to get royal licenses. France burned banned books publicly.

discovery.text: The First Amendment in 1791 was revolutionary — a government voluntarily protecting press freedom.

twist.text: Even with legal protections, governments have always found indirect ways to suppress media.

climax.text: The battle between press freedom and state control has never ended — it just moved online.

punchline.text: Free press is always under construction.

quiz.question: What was revolutionary about the First Amendment?
options: A government voluntarily protected press freedom
